## Natural history notes

A small, flat-headed sparrow characterized by its short tail, buffy-orange face, pale central crown stripe, and fine dark streaking on the back and sides. In Florida, it is found in open grasslands, dry prairies, pastures, pine flatwoods, and other grassy habitats with low vegetation and scattered bare ground. It feeds mainly on grasshoppers, beetles, caterpillars, spiders, and seeds, usually foraging low on the ground while remaining hidden in dense grasses.
